items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: the very first album I had, Bud Shank on alto and Clay Jenkins on trumpet

ctx.x: Said he heard it from Maria Schneider, who heard it from Bob Brookmeyer, okay? I’m tracing the lineage. And the statement was, from Brookmeyer, you should try to hold off as long as you can in an arrangement before you pass it to a soloist. So my question is do you agree with that, and the follow-up is have you ever felt like you want to give soloists some guidance for the way they’re going to solo on this chart that you’ve spent many hours working on?

Just the opposite. As a matter of fact I don’t agree with Bobby. Bobby at one point made the statement that a jazz arrangement could be jazz without improvisation. The creative art of manipulating notes in a jazz style was enough without improvisation. To me the chart is just a vehicle. It’s just a skeleton to get the improvisation out there. So my focus is the jazz improvisation. And like for instance when I wrote for — the very first album I had, Bud Shank on alto and Clay Jenkins on trumpet and I did a Horace…
Yes, the one I was listening to last night, I think it was Clay playing on it. And he had a lot of space, as did the tenor player who followed him.
